reasons.D: Keeps the editorial 'we', verbless descriptive fragments and semicolon-joined asides ('Stout; decidedly stout.') that match the passage's clipped, gossipy movement; a touch heavy on the whimsy but closest in stance and rhythm.
reasons.B: Short declaratives and abrupt turns ('So I shall go on.', 'He was stout.') echo the passage's choppy rhythm and dry humour, but the first-person 'I' and fuller sentences lose the mock-editorial stance.
reasons.A: Measured, balanced periodic sentences and a polished essayistic tone with neat antitheses; competent period feel but smoother and more literary than the passage's jotted, fragmentary manner.
reasons.C: Argumentative 'Consider...' structure, flowing modern phrasing and tidy transitions read as a smooth contemporary essayist, furthest from the passage's clipped, qualifier-laden gossip.
